memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You shall not misuse the name of the Lord your God, for the Lord will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name. - Deut 5:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's name stands for His character, His reputation, everything He is. To "misuse" His name is to treat that holy name carelessly — using it as a thoughtless curse word, swearing false oaths by it, or claiming His authority for things He never approved. In the ancient world a name carried weight; to speak God's name was to invoke the living God Himself. He tells His people plainly: do not treat My name as empty or common.

This command reaches deeper than avoiding bad language, important as that is. Anyone who bears God's name in public — and every believer does — represents Him to a watching world. We can misuse His name by claiming to belong to Him while living in a way that dishonours Him, or by attaching "God told me" to our own desires. The name is holy; how we carry it matters.

There is good news wrapped inside this warning. In Christ, we have been given the highest privilege of all: we are called by His name, adopted as children of God (1 John 3:1). The One whose name we could never honour perfectly honoured the Father completely on our behalf. Now, gratefully, let your words and your life treat His name as the treasure it is. When people hear you speak of God, may they meet reverence, not carelessness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do my everyday words treat God's name as holy or as common?
- In what ways might my life either honour or dishonour the name I carry as a Christian?
- Have I ever attached "God said" to something that was really just my own wish?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, Your name is holy, and by grace I am called by it. Guard my lips and my life so that I honour Your name in the world, never treating as common what is holy. Amen.
